newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on speculative buying by retail investors but the future market trend was still unclear, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,200 yuan ($385) per tonne, rising 58 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,144.
May rose 20 to 3,208, July 28 to 3,279, September was unchanged at 3,278 and November increased two to 3,370.
Combined volume rose to 25,100 tonnes from 9,200.
Traders said speculative buying dominated today's trading with open interest rising.
"Speculation was the main reason for the day's rises, but increases in open interest indicated the differing views on the market amongst investors are moving further apart," one trader said.
Analysts said soybeans were unlikely to rise further in the next few days given the lack of large-scale follow-up buying.
